text: Augment the existing factorization-machine scorer with leakage-safe sequential user-history features computed strictly from training events preceding each impression: exponentially decayed counts of prior long-view positives and negatives plus time since the most recent positive interaction; keep pointwise BCE training, the current request-context fields, split, and evaluation protocol unchanged.
rationale: The current model reaches primary 0.6029, but diagnostics show persistent weaknesses for long-duration impressions (primary 0.5234), several time/context slices, and users with zero validation positives (primary 0.25). Static user/item and request-context fields cannot represent changing intent, while sequential history is a distinct, testable source of signal. Build each feature using only events earlier than the target impression, fit any decay or clipping constants on training data only, and use bounded aggregates to control runtime and leakage risk. The hypothesis is that recent positive history improves personalization and recent negative history suppresses poor candidates, increasing within-user GAUC and nDCG@5; evaluate primary as the stopping objective while checking classification, all ranking diagnostics, score distribution, and segment diagnostics for broad rather than purely global gains.
